subject: Re: DPA Annex — telemetry proxying & sandboxing questions
messages:
From: Jai Singh <j.singh@medivault.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: security-assessments@medivault.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SSQ: telemetry exports, proxying, and sandboxing

Hi Connor / Kimberly,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we prepare the DPA annex and the security questionnaire, a couple of follow-ups from our privacy team:

1) Telemetry export boundary — can you confirm whether request/response telemetry that hits Redwood hosted endpoints ever includes raw PII (names, emails, SSNs) in logs or traces that we would classify as exportable personal data? If so, what redaction/tokenization is applied before logs leave the serving plane?

2) Edge sandboxing / proxying — we saw mention on your architecture page about an "edge sandbox" for untrusted models. Does that sandbox perform full request-side pseudonymization (prefix hashing) before telemetry/observability events are emitted to your hosted telemetry pipeline?

3) Subprocessors — we need an explicit list of any telemetry vendors who receive aggregated or sampled traces (SaaS), plus whether those vendors can reconstruct request context.

Attached: our SSQ template (first pass). Could you provide a short answer set and a labelled dataflow diagram showing where PII is present, where it's redacted, and which subprocessors see which slices?

Best,
Jai
Jai Singh | Senior Counsel, Privacy
MediVault Health

Attachments: medivault-ssq.csv

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jai Singh <j.singh@medivault.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SSQ: telemetry exports, proxying, and sandboxing

Hi Jai — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary while we gather artifacts:

- Short answer: Redwood does not intentionally log PII in plaintext in long-term telemetry. We apply request-level redaction and a two-tiered tokenization pipeline for identifiers before most telemetry leaves the serving layer.
- Edge sandboxing: the sandbox can be configured to run a lightweight obfuscation pass (prefix-hash + truncate) before telemetry is emitted; by default the sandbox keeps raw payloads in-memory only and writes obfuscated traces to observability backends.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide a canonical inventory (names + access scope) — there are three telemetry vendors we push aggregated metrics to, and one caching vendor that gets non-identifying request metadata for debugging.

I'll loop in Kimberly and Marissa for the diagram and the DPA annex redline. Expect a filled SSQ and a labelled PNG by EOD Thursday.

Connor
Director, Privacy Integrations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 14:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: mapping for MediVault — telemetry slices and subprocessors

Connor / Marissa — draft notes for what we'll send: please review inline.

- Serving plane: incoming requests (user prompt + metadata) are processed on GPUs; we maintain a short-lived KV cache; raw prompts are encrypted at rest for retention <24h. Long-term observability events are generated by an async pipeline that pulls from a sanitized event stream.

- Redaction / tokenization: two passes — (1) in-proxy regex redaction for obvious PII fields, (2) deterministic tokenization for stable identifiers (email -> token hash) stored in a key-managed index. Keys are KMS-wrapped and rotate quarterly.

- Edge sandbox/ proxy: sandbox runs in an isolated container group. If MediVault requires, we can enable an extra proxy shim that drops free-text fields entirely and emits only high-level metrics. Note: this will increase false-negative signal for model quality monitoring.

- Subprocessors: list to include (1) Observix Inc. (aggregated traces, no raw payload), (2) CacheFlow (request metadata for cache misses), (3) LogKeep (brief access to redacted traces for triage). I'll attach the labeled diagram next.

Thanks — Kimberly

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-diagram-v3.png (draft)

From: Jai Singh <j.singh@medivault.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: clarifying reconstructability of identifiers

Hi Kimberly / Connor,

Thanks for the quick notes — helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs from our security team:

- Deterministic tokenization: is the mapping reversible by Redwood (i.e., do you keep an index that allows you to map token -> original identifier on demand)? If so, what controls govern access to that mapping?

- Subprocessor access: for LogKeep and CacheFlow, can these vendors see the token mapping or only the hashed tokens? We need attestations that subprocessors cannot rehydrate PII from telemetry slices.

- Evidence: please provide a short excerpt of your access logs (redacted) showing a KMS operation and a triage session where a redacted trace was viewed, with timestamps. A CSV or anonymized log snippet will work.

Best,
Jai

Attachments: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jai Singh <j.singh@medivault.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Mar 2028 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: clarifying reconstructability of identifiers

Hi Jai — quick answers and attached evidence bundle (see drive link and attached PNG):

- Mapping reversibility: Redwood maintains a reversible mapping for deterministic tokens in a KMS-wrapped index used only for support triage and compliance requests. Access is strictly role-based (Support Tier-3 + Compliance) and gated by an internal approval workflow that logs a justification and approver.

- Subprocessors: Observix and CacheFlow receive only salted hashes (non-reversible) for aggregated metrics. LogKeep has access to redacted traces only; they do NOT receive the mapping or raw identifiers. We have contractual clauses prohibiting re-identification.

- Evidence: attached redwood-dataflow-diagram-v3.png and a sanitized CSV with an access-log snippet showing a KMS Decrypt event and the support ticket ID. Redactions have been applied to principal names.

Link: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/DEAL-5821/dataflow-v3

If that looks good, Connor / Kimberly — I'll push the DPA proposed redline (docx) and a short explanation of the sandbox proxy option (opt-in boolean) for MediVault to review.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Security Program Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-diagram-v3.png, access-log-snippet.csv
